# Twyne — Voice, Adaptive Interview, Live Rubric, and the Room That Reads As You Write

## Context

Four connected weaknesses in the writing workspace, all of which come down to the
same thing: the room is **inert and static**. It only acts when clicked, and when
it does act it measures shape rather than substance.

1. **The rubric is structurally unable to punish thin or off-target writing.**
   `buildCriteria()` (`src/components/rubric/rubric-panel.tsx:788`) returns ten
   hardcoded criteria. Four of them — Organization, Pacing, Vocabulary, Paragraph
   Shape — are computed entirely by `scoreStaticFeatures()`
   (`src/utils/rubric.ts:59`) from sentence-length variance, type-token ratio and
   paragraph word counts. **None of them ever see the brief.** Well-paced,
   lexically varied, nicely-paragraphed off-topic filler scores 10/10 on three
   categories, and `combineJudgesAndStatic()` (`src/utils/rubric.ts:512`) folds
   that in at a flat `STATIC_WEIGHT = 0.2`. A poem is graded on citation density;
   a memo on type-token ratio. The criteria set is also unchangeable by the writer.

2. **The side panel is pull-only.** Cast, Rubric, Marginalia and Apparatus all sit
   idle until the writer presses a button. Nothing accumulates, nothing signals.
   The editors read the whole draft cold on every convene, and never see the
   *trajectory* of the writing.

3. **The interview asks seven free-text questions and nothing else.** Both the
   static form (`STEPS`, `src/components/onboarding/anti-tabula-rasa.tsx:24`) and
   the conversational interview produce the same seven prose strings
   (`ProjectInterviewAnswers`). No structured signal reaches the judges.

4. **Voice is built and disconnected.** `convex/voice.ts:synthesizeSpeech` (Pro-gated,
   rate-limited), `runClientVoiceSpeech()` (`src/utils/ai-client.ts:322`, BYOK),
   the per-feature voice/speed/instructions settings UI
   (`src/routes/settings/index.tsx:1873`) and the pricing copy all exist. **There
   is not a single caller.** Speech-to-text does not exist at all.

**Intended outcome:** the editors comment continuously as you write and carry the
memory of how the draft got here; the rubric grades against *this* piece with
criteria you can edit; the interview adapts its question types; and the room can
be heard and spoken to.

### Decisions taken

- **STT:** server + BYOK transcription (mirrors the existing `synthesizeSpeech`
  pattern). Works everywhere and retains the audio, so a voice note is really voice.
- **Rubric:** fixed spine keeping the majority of today's criteria, plus
  writer-defined custom criteria, plus a relevance gate.
- **Background room:** all five editors, on a real delta of **~300 new words** *and*
  **2 minutes of inactivity**.
- **Side panel:** enrich the four existing tabs in place. No new tab.

---

## A. Voice

### A1. Hear the editors (wire the existing TTS)

Almost entirely a wiring job — no new provider code.

- **New `src/utils/speech.ts`** — a module-level playback manager: one `HTMLAudioElement`
  at a time (starting a new read stops the current one), an object-URL cache keyed by
  `hash(text) + voice` so re-playing a note is free, and a `twyne:speech` status event
  for UI state. Public surface: `speak({ text, voice, instructions })`, `stopSpeech()`,
  `speechState()`.
- **Provider chain**, matching every other feature in the app: BYOK
  `runClientVoiceSpeech()` first → Convex `api.voice.synthesizeSpeech` (returns
  `audioBase64` + `mimeType`; decode to a Blob) → structured `AppError` via
  `createAppError("CONFIGURATION_ERROR")` with a `recovery.action` of
  `"choose-provider"`. Note the Convex path is **Pro-gated** (`convex/voice.ts:49`) —
  surface that as an upsell notice, not a failure.
- **Per-editor voices.** Add `speechVoice?: string` to `Persona`
  (`src/types/index.ts:1`) and assign one to each of the five in
  `src/utils/personas.ts` (e.g. `devil: "onyx"`, `angel: "shimmer"`,
  `scholar: "echo"`, `editor: "ash"`, `reader: "alloy"`). Pass the persona's
  existing `voice` lore string as the TTS `instructions` parameter — it is already
  written as a voice-direction paragraph and is exactly what that field wants.
- **New `src/components/ui/speak-button.tsx`** — a small `component$` taking
  `text`, `voice`, `instructions`; renders play/stop/loading, `aria-label`s properly,
  reuses `ApplicationNotice` for errors.
- **Wire into:** each note card and the analysis memos/synthesis in
  `personas-panel.tsx`; the narrative review in `rubric-panel.tsx` (guarded on
  `store.result.review`); persona replies in `comments-panel.tsx`. Also a
  "read the selection" item on the editor's selection bubble in `twyne-editor.tsx`.

### A2. Voice notes (record → keep audio → transcribe)

- **New Convex action `transcribeSpeech`** in `convex/voice.ts` — same skeleton as
  `synthesizeSpeech`: identity check, `consumeRateLimit` with a new
  `RATE_LIMITS.voiceTranscribe` entry (`convex/lib/rateLimit.ts:151`), Pro check via
  `isProSubscription`, then `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` (multipart, model
  `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`) using `VOICE_OPENAI_API_KEY ?? OPENAI_API_KEY`. Accepts
  `audioBase64` + `mimeType`, returns `{ text, provider, model }`.
- **BYOK twin `runClientVoiceTranscribe()`** in `src/utils/ai-client.ts`, beside
  `runClientVoiceSpeech` (line 322) — same `resolveFeatureConfig` /
  `isOpenAiCompatibleProvider` guard. Register a new `"voice-transcription"`
  `AiFeature` and give it a label/description in `src/routes/settings/index.tsx:123`
  so it appears in the per-feature override UI like every other feature.
- **New `src/utils/voice-notes.ts`** — `MediaRecorder` wrapper (`audio/webm;codecs=opus`),
  permission handling, duration cap (~3 min), level metering for a waveform, plus
  IDB persistence of the Blob.
- **IDB migration.** `src/utils/idb.ts` is at `DB_VERSION = 1` (line 31) with an
  `upgrade` that adds stores conditionally (lines 70–92). Bump to `2` and add a
  `voice-notes` store inside the same guarded block — the existing
  `if (!db.objectStoreNames.contains(...))` pattern makes this a safe additive
  migration for existing users.
- **Attach to Marginalia.** Extend `UserComment` (`src/utils/user-comments.ts:34`)
  with optional `audioId`, `audioDurationMs`, `transcriptProvider`. A voice note is
  a normal comment whose `text` is the transcript, with playback attached — so
  threading, resolution, @-mentions and persona replies all work unchanged.
- **UI:** a mic button in the `comments-panel.tsx` composer and on the editor's
  selection bubble. Record → waveform → stop → transcribe → **show the transcript
  editable before saving** (transcription is never perfect and the writer should own
  the words). Keep the audio either way.

### A3. Voice interview

- Push-to-talk button in the `ConversationalInterview` composer
  (`conversational-interview.tsx:742`). Records → transcribes → **fills
  `store.draft`** rather than auto-sending, so the writer edits before it goes.
- Optional "read questions aloud" toggle: when on, each new `interviewer` message
  is passed to `speak()` from A1 with a neutral voice. Persist the toggle via
  `saveMetaToIdb("interview-read-aloud", …)`.
- Works in both `first-run` and `refine` modes with no branching.

---

## B. Interview variety — structured probes

**The idea:** alongside the seven prose fields, the interviewer generates a handful
of *typed* questions from what it has already learned, and the structured answers
become first-class evidence for the judges.

- **New types** in `src/types/index.ts`:
  ```ts
  export type ProbeKind = "choice" | "multi" | "blanks" | "scale";
  export interface DossierProbe {
    id: string;
    kind: ProbeKind;
    prompt: string;
    /** choice/multi */ options?: string[];
    /** blanks: "The reader should leave ___ and do ___." */ template?: string;
    /** scale */ min?: number; max?: number; minLabel?: string; maxLabel?: string;
    answer?: string | string[] | number;
    /** Which brief field this sharpens, when it maps to one. */
    relatesTo?: keyof ProjectInterviewAnswers;
  }
  ```
  Add `probes?: DossierProbe[]` to `ProjectBrief` — **optional**, so every existing
  saved brief keeps working untouched.
- **Prompt contract.** Extend `interviewSystemPrompt()` (`convex/agents.ts:473`) to
  allow a third tagged segment, `PROBE:`, carrying one `DossierProbe` as JSON —
  alongside the existing `DOSSIER:` and `SYNTHESIZE:` tags. Parsing reuses
  `extractTaggedJson` / `stripTaggedJson` from `src/utils/llm-parsing.ts` exactly as
  `parseInterviewTurnResult()` (`convex/agents.ts:519`) already does, so this is an
  additive branch, not a rewrite. Instruct the model to reach for a probe when a
  prose answer was vague, and to keep probes concrete and answerable in one tap.
- Mirror the same parsing in the BYOK path, `runClientInterviewTurn()`
  (`src/utils/ai-client.ts:1651`), so both paths behave identically.
- **Rendering** in `conversational-interview.tsx`: chips for `choice`/`multi`,
  inline inputs inside the sentence for `blanks`, a slider for `scale`. Answering a
  probe sends a synthesised writer turn (`"Format: dispatch"`) *and* stores the
  structured `DossierProbe` — so the transcript stays readable and the data stays typed.
  Show answered probes in the existing "Room brief" sidebar (line 636).
- **The static form gets them too.** Add a `kind: "probes"` step to `STEPS`
  (`anti-tabula-rasa.tsx:24`) as a new "Dept. of Particulars" between the current
  VII and VIII. On entry it calls the interviewer once with the answers filled so
  far and renders 3–5 generated probes. This is literally "generated based on the
  last form". If the call fails, the step self-skips — the form must never block on
  a network call.
- **Feed the judgement.** `buildUserPrompt()` (`convex/agentPrompts.ts:148`) gains a
  `PARTICULARS` block rendering answered probes after the brief block. Because
  every judge (`judgeRoom`, `judgeEvidence`, `judgeSufficiency`, `conveneRoom`,
  `analyzeRoom`) builds its prompt through this one function, they all pick it up
  from a single edit.

---

## C. Rubric — fixed spine, writer-owned criteria, relevance gate

### C1. The gate (this is the actual bug fix)

- **New `judgeTargetFit` action** in `convex/agents.ts`, modelled on
  `judgeSufficiency` (line 1498): scores 1–10 for *"does this content serve **this**
  audience and **this** goal at all, in **this** format?"* — independent of how well
  written it is. BYOK twin `runClientTargetFitJudge()` in `ai-client.ts` alongside
  `runClientEvidenceJudge` (line 872).
- **Cap the shape scores by relevance.** In `rubric-panel.tsx:buildCriteria`, every
  criterion sourced purely from `scoreStaticFeatures` gets:
  ```ts
  const shapeCeiling = 3 + targetFit * 0.7;  // targetFit 2 → ceiling 4.4; 9 → 9.3
  score = Math.min(rawShapeScore, shapeCeiling);
  ```
  and its feedback string says plainly that the ceiling was applied and why.
  Elegant filler can no longer bank 10/10 on Pacing.
- **Gate the aggregate too.** `combineJudgesAndStatic()` (`src/utils/rubric.ts:512`)
  takes a new `targetFit` argument and replaces the flat `STATIC_WEIGHT = 0.2` with
  a relevance-scaled weight (`0.2 * targetFit / 10`), redistributing the remainder
  onto `minJudge`. Well-shaped irrelevance stops being able to lift the grade. This
  function has direct unit tests — extend them (see Verification).

### C2. Fixed spine + writer-defined criteria

- **The spine keeps the majority of today's criteria** so scores stay comparable
  across runs: Thesis & Argument, Evidence & Support, Sufficiency & Development,
  Bullshit Resistance, Organization & Flow, Voice & Tone, Reader Engagement, plus a
  new **Target Fit** fed by C1. Pacing, Vocabulary and Paragraph Shape are
  **demoted from scored criteria to a collapsible "Measured features" diagnostics
  block** — they are genuinely useful information about shape, and genuinely bad
  grades. They still render, with their numbers, below the criteria.
- **Writer-defined criteria.** New `RubricCriterionSpec { id, label, description,
  weight, source: "spine" | "custom" }` in `src/types/index.ts`, persisted through
  the existing `saveMetaToIdb("rubric-criteria", …)` helper
  (`src/utils/idb.ts:614`) — no schema change needed. A small editor in
  `rubric-panel.tsx` (and the fuller `/rubric` route) lets the writer add, rename,
  reweight, or disable a criterion.
- **New generic `judgeCustomCriterion` action** in `convex/agents.ts` — takes
  `{ brief, draftText, label, description }`, returns the same
  `{score, rationale}` JSON contract, parsed by the existing `parseJudgeOutput`.
  Custom criteria are fanned out in parallel like `judgeRoom` does.
- **Suggested criteria.** A "Suggest criteria for this piece" button calls a new
  `suggestRubricCriteria` action that reads the brief (including the B probes) and
  proposes 3–5 criteria fitted to the format. They are **proposals the writer
  accepts into their set** — never applied silently. This gets the adaptivity
  without losing run-to-run comparability.

### C3. Score history

- Persist each run as an append-only `rubric-history` entry via `saveMetaToIdb`
  (`{ at, overall, grade, perCriterion }`, capped at ~50). Feeds the sparkline in E.

---

## D. The background room — five editors reading as you write

Modelled directly on `src/utils/background-research.ts`, which already solves the
debounce / dedupe / status-event / soft-cap problem well.

- **New `src/utils/draft-trajectory.ts`**
  - `diffParagraphs(prev, next)` → `{ added: string[], removed: number, netWords: number }`,
    matching on normalised paragraph text.
  - An append-only trajectory log in IDB (`saveMetaToIdb("draft-trajectory", …)`,
    capped ~60 entries, per folio): `{ at, netWords, addedCount, removedCount, excerpt }`.
  - `trajectoryDigest(entries, max = 12)` → a compact prose summary
    (*"Over the last hour: +740 words, four paragraphs added around the funding
    argument, the opening anecdote cut."*) That digest is the "path of the edits"
    the room needs.

- **New `src/utils/background-room.ts`** — same shape as `background-research.ts`
  (`startBackgroundRoom` / `stopBackgroundRoom` / `onDraftChanged` /
  `kickBackgroundRoom` / `snapshot`), with the agreed trigger:
  - accumulate net-new words since the last pass; arm only at **≥ 300**;
  - then wait for **120 s of no `twyne:content` events** (each keystroke resets the
    idle timer — this is an *idle* timer, not a debounce);
  - a hard floor of 5 min between passes and a per-session cap (~8) so a long
    session can't run away with spend;
  - skip entirely when the draft is below `MIN_EDITOR_WORDS` (80), reusing
    `draftReadiness` from `src/utils/draft-thresholds.ts`.
  - **All five editors** via `api.agents.conveneRoom` (BYOK `runClientAgent` first,
    same order as `personas-panel.tsx:562`). `RATE_LIMITS.agentRoom` is 6/min
    (`convex/lib/rateLimit.ts:167`) — a ≥5-minute floor sits comfortably inside it.
  - The pass sends the **new material as the anchor context plus the trajectory
    digest**, not a cold re-read of the whole draft.
  - Emits `twyne:background-room` status events, mirroring `twyne:background-research`.

- **Prompt support.** Add `trajectory?: string` and `newMaterial?: string` to
  `AgentRequest` (`convex/agentPrompts.ts:41`) and render them in `buildUserPrompt`
  as a `SINCE YOUR LAST READ` block, with a task line directing the note at the new
  material while staying aware of the whole piece. Add the matching optional
  validators to `personaValidator`'s siblings in `convex/agents.ts`.

- **Notes land as a distinct class.** Add `origin?: "convened" | "background"` to
  `PersonaFeedback` (`src/types/index.ts:24`). Background notes persist through the
  existing `savePersonaNoteLocally` (`src/utils/convex-sync.ts:606`) and
  `api.sync.putPersonaNote` path, and pin inline through the existing
  `twyne:persona-notes` event with a lighter mark style.

- **Trajectory feeds the explicit actions too.** When the writer *does* press
  Convene, or Send to copyedit, the digest goes along — so the deliberate pass is
  cheaper and better informed, which is the payoff you asked for.

- **Wiring:** `src/routes/editor/index.tsx:406` already starts
  `startBackgroundResearch` inside `useVisibleTask$` and tears it down in `cleanup`.
  Start and stop the background room in exactly the same place, and add a settings
  toggle (default **on**, but honour a "quiet" off switch) stored in `RoomSettings`
  (`src/types/index.ts:341`) so it syncs through the existing
  `api.sync.putRoomSettings` path.

---

## E. Side panel — enriched in place

No new tab. `src/routes/editor/index.tsx:1038` already renders `panelTabs` and keeps
all four panels mounted-but-hidden (lines 1088–1124), so badges and passive updates
work without touching the mount strategy.

- **Tab badges.** Extend `PanelTab` with a live unread count. A tiny
  `src/utils/panel-activity.ts` counts unseen items per panel from the events
  already flying (`twyne:persona-notes`, `twyne:background-sources`,
  `twyne:user-comments-changed`, and the new `twyne:background-room`), clearing on
  tab activation. Render as a small accented dot/count on the tab in the existing
  accent colour.
- **Cast:** background notes render as quieter "passing notes" (lighter rule, no
  heavy card chrome, `origin` label), grouped under a **"Since you last convened"**

  `twyne:background-room` state ("the room read your last three paragraphs, 4m ago").
- **Rubric:** a compact sparkline of `rubric-history` (C3) under the grade circle,
  the "Measured features" diagnostics block (C2), and the criteria editor.
- **Marginalia:** voice notes with inline playback + waveform (A2); mic button in

- **Apparatus:** unchanged apart from picking up the shared badge.

Four connected weaknesses in the writing workspace, all of which come down to the
same thing: the room is **inert and static**. It only acts when clicked, and when
it does act it measures shape rather than substance.

1. **The rubric is structurally unable to punish thin or off-target writing.**
   `buildCriteria()` (`src/components/rubric/rubric-panel.tsx:788`) returns ten
   hardcoded criteria. Four of them — Organization, Pacing, Vocabulary, Paragraph
   Shape — are computed entirely by `scoreStaticFeatures()`
   (`src/utils/rubric.ts:59`) from sentence-length variance, type-token ratio and
   paragraph word counts. **None of them ever see the brief.** Well-paced,
   lexically varied, nicely-paragraphed off-topic filler scores 10/10 on three
   categories, and `combineJudgesAndStatic()` (`src/utils/rubric.ts:512`) folds
   that in at a flat `STATIC_WEIGHT = 0.2`. A poem is graded on citation density;
   a memo on type-token ratio. The criteria set is also unchangeable by the writer.

2. **The side panel is pull-only.** Cast, Rubric, Marginalia and Apparatus all sit
   idle until the writer presses a button. Nothing accumulates, nothing signals.
   The editors read the whole draft cold on every convene, and never see the
   *trajectory* of the writing.

   static form (`STEPS`, `src/components/onboarding/anti-tabula-rasa.tsx:24`) and

# Twyne — Voice, Adaptive Interview, Live Rubric, and the Room That Reads As You Write

## Context

Four connected weaknesses in the writing workspace, all of which come down to the
same thing: the room is **inert and static**. It only acts when clicked, and when
it does act it measures shape rather than substance.

1. **The rubric is structurally unable to punish thin or off-target writing.**
   `buildCriteria()` (`src/components/rubric/rubric-panel.tsx:788`) returns ten
   hardcoded criteria. Four of them — Organization, Pacing, Vocabulary, Paragraph
   Shape — are computed entirely by `scoreStaticFeatures()`
   (`src/utils/rubric.ts:59`) from sentence-length variance, type-token ratio and
   paragraph word counts. **None of them ever see the brief.** Well-paced,
   lexically varied, nicely-paragraphed off-topic filler scores 10/10 on three
   categories, and `combineJudgesAndStatic()` (`src/utils/rubric.ts:512`) folds
   that in at a flat `STATIC_WEIGHT = 0.2`. A poem is graded on citation density;
   a memo on type-token ratio. The criteria set is also unchangeable by the writer.

2. **The side panel is pull-only.** Cast, Rubric, Marginalia and Apparatus all sit
   idle until the writer presses a button. Nothing accumulates, nothing signals.
   The editors read the whole draft cold on every convene, and never see the
   *trajectory* of the writing.

3. **The interview asks seven free-text questions and nothing else.** Both the
   static form (`STEPS`, `src/components/onboarding/anti-tabula-rasa.tsx:24`) and
   the conversational interview produce the same seven prose strings
   (`ProjectInterviewAnswers`). No structured signal reaches the judges.

4. **Voice is built and disconnected.** `convex/voice.ts:synthesizeSpeech` (Pro-gated,
   rate-limited), `runClientVoiceSpeech()` (`src/utils/ai-client.ts:322`, BYOK),
   the per-feature voice/speed/instructions settings UI
   (`src/routes/settings/index.tsx:1873`) and the pricing copy all exist. **There
   is not a single caller.** Speech-to-text does not exist at all.

**Intended outcome:** the editors comment continuously as you write and carry the
memory of how the draft got here; the rubric grades against *this* piece with
criteria you can edit; the interview adapts its question types; and the room can
be heard and spoken to.

### Decisions taken

- **STT:** server + BYOK transcription (mirrors the existing `synthesizeSpeech`
  pattern). Works everywhere and retains the audio, so a voice note is really voice.
- **Rubric:** fixed spine keeping the majority of today's criteria, plus
  writer-defined custom criteria, plus a relevance gate.
- **Background room:** all five editors, on a real delta of **~300 new words** *and*
  **2 minutes of inactivity**.
- **Side panel:** enrich the four existing tabs in place. No new tab.

---

## A. Voice

### A1. Hear the editors (wire the existing TTS)

Almost entirely a wiring job — no new provider code.

- **New `src/utils/speech.ts`** — a module-level playback manager: one `HTMLAudioElement`
  at a time (starting a new read stops the current one), an object-URL cache keyed by
  `hash(text) + voice` so re-playing a note is free, and a `twyne:speech` status event
  for UI state. Public surface: `speak({ text, voice, instructions })`, `stopSpeech()`,
  `speechState()`.
- **Provider chain**, matching every other feature in the app: BYOK
  `runClientVoiceSpeech()` first → Convex `api.voice.synthesizeSpeech` (returns
  `audioBase64` + `mimeType`; decode to a Blob) → structured `AppError` via
  `createAppError("CONFIGURATION_ERROR")` with a `recovery.action` of
  `"choose-provider"`. Note the Convex path is **Pro-gated** (`convex/voice.ts:49`) —
  surface that as an upsell notice, not a failure.
- **Per-editor voices.** Add `speechVoice?: string` to `Persona`
  (`src/types/index.ts:1`) and assign one to each of the five in
  `src/utils/personas.ts` (e.g. `devil: "onyx"`, `angel: "shimmer"`,
  `scholar: "echo"`, `editor: "ash"`, `reader: "alloy"`). Pass the persona's
  existing `voice` lore string as the TTS `instructions` parameter — it is already
  written as a voice-direction paragraph and is exactly what that field wants.
- **New `src/components/ui/speak-button.tsx`** — a small `component$` taking
  `text`, `voice`, `instructions`; renders play/stop/loading, `aria-label`s properly,
  reuses `ApplicationNotice` for errors.
- **Wire into:** each note card and the analysis memos/synthesis in
  `personas-panel.tsx`; the narrative review in `rubric-panel.tsx` (guarded on
  `store.result.review`); persona replies in `comments-panel.tsx`. Also a
  "read the selection" item on the editor's selection bubble in `twyne-editor.tsx`.

### A2. Voice notes (record → keep audio → transcribe)

- **New Convex action `transcribeSpeech`** in `convex/voice.ts` — same skeleton as
  `synthesizeSpeech`: identity check, `consumeRateLimit` with a new
  `RATE_LIMITS.voiceTranscribe` entry (`convex/lib/rateLimit.ts:151`), Pro check via
  `isProSubscription`, then `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` (multipart, model
  `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`) using `VOICE_OPENAI_API_KEY ?? OPENAI_API_KEY`. Accepts
  `audioBase64` + `mimeType`, returns `{ text, provider, model }`.
- **BYOK twin `runClientVoiceTranscribe()`** in `src/utils/ai-client.ts`, beside
  `runClientVoiceSpeech` (line 322) — same `resolveFeatureConfig` /
  `isOpenAiCompatibleProvider` guard. Register a new `"voice-transcription"`
  `AiFeature` and give it a label/description in `src/routes/settings/index.tsx:123`
  so it appears in the per-feature override UI like every other feature.
- **New `src/utils/voice-notes.ts`** — `MediaRecorder` wrapper (`audio/webm;codecs=opus`),
  permission handling, duration cap (~3 min), level metering for a waveform, plus
  IDB persistence of the Blob.
- **IDB migration.** `src/utils/idb.ts` is at `DB_VERSION = 1` (line 31) with an
  `upgrade` that adds stores conditionally (lines 70–92). Bump to `2` and add a
  `voice-notes` store inside the same guarded block — the existing
  `if (!db.objectStoreNames.contains(...))` pattern makes this a safe additive
  migration for existing users.
- **Attach to Marginalia.** Extend `UserComment` (`src/utils/user-comments.ts:34`)
  with optional `audioId`, `audioDurationMs`, `transcriptProvider`. A voice note is
  a normal comment whose `text` is the transcript, with playback attached — so
  threading, resolution, @-mentions and persona replies all work unchanged.
- **UI:** a mic button in the `comments-panel.tsx` composer and on the editor's
  selection bubble. Record → waveform → stop → transcribe → **show the transcript
  editable before saving** (transcription is never perfect and the writer should own
  the words). Keep the audio either way.

### A3. Voice interview

- Push-to-talk button in the `ConversationalInterview` composer
  (`conversational-interview.tsx:742`). Records → transcribes → **fills
  `store.draft`** rather than auto-sending, so the writer edits before it goes.
- Optional "read questions aloud" toggle: when on, each new `interviewer` message
  is passed to `speak()` from A1 with a neutral voice. Persist the toggle via
  `saveMetaToIdb("interview-read-aloud", …)`.
- Works in both `first-run` and `refine` modes with no branching.

---

## B. Interview variety — structured probes

**The idea:** alongside the seven prose fields, the interviewer generates a handful
of *typed* questions from what it has already learned, and the structured answers
become first-class evidence for the judges.

- **New types** in `src/types/index.ts`:
  ```ts
  export type ProbeKind = "choice" | "multi" | "blanks" | "scale";
  export interface DossierProbe {
    id: string;
    kind: ProbeKind;
    prompt: string;
    /** choice/multi */ options?: string[];
    /** blanks: "The reader should leave ___ and do ___." */ template?: string;
    /** scale */ min?: number; max?: number; minLabel?: string; maxLabel?: string;
    answer?: string | string[] | number;
    /** Which brief field this sharpens, when it maps to one. */
    relatesTo?: keyof ProjectInterviewAnswers;
  }
  ```
  Add `probes?: DossierProbe[]` to `ProjectBrief` — **optional**, so every existing
  saved brief keeps working untouched.
- **Prompt contract.** Extend `interviewSystemPrompt()` (`convex/agents.ts:473`) to
  allow a third tagged segment, `PROBE:`, carrying one `DossierProbe` as JSON —
  alongside the existing `DOSSIER:` and `SYNTHESIZE:` tags. Parsing reuses
  `extractTaggedJson` / `stripTaggedJson` from `src/utils/llm-parsing.ts` exactly as
  `parseInterviewTurnResult()` (`convex/agents.ts:519`) already does, so this is an
  additive branch, not a rewrite. Instruct the model to reach for a probe when a
  prose answer was vague, and to keep probes concrete and answerable in one tap.
- Mirror the same parsing in the BYOK path, `runClientInterviewTurn()`
  (`src/utils/ai-client.ts:1651`), so both paths behave identically.
- **Rendering** in `conversational-interview.tsx`: chips for `choice`/`multi`,
  inline inputs inside the sentence for `blanks`, a slider for `scale`. Answering a
  probe sends a synthesised writer turn (`"Format: dispatch"`) *and* stores the
  structured `DossierProbe` — so the transcript stays readable and the data stays typed.
  Show answered probes in the existing "Room brief" sidebar (line 636).
- **The static form gets them too.** Add a `kind: "probes"` step to `STEPS`
  (`anti-tabula-rasa.tsx:24`) as a new "Dept. of Particulars" between the current
  VII and VIII. On entry it calls the interviewer once with the answers filled so
  far and renders 3–5 generated probes. This is literally "generated based on the
  last form". If the call fails, the step self-skips — the form must never block on
  a network call.
- **Feed the judgement.** `buildUserPrompt()` (`convex/agentPrompts.ts:148`) gains a
  `PARTICULARS` block rendering answered probes after the brief block. Because
  every judge (`judgeRoom`, `judgeEvidence`, `judgeSufficiency`, `conveneRoom`,
  `analyzeRoom`) builds its prompt through this one function, they all pick it up
  from a single edit.

---

## C. Rubric — fixed spine, writer-owned criteria, relevance gate

### C1. The gate (this is the actual bug fix)

- **New `judgeTargetFit` action** in `convex/agents.ts`, modelled on
  `judgeSufficiency` (line 1498): scores 1–10 for *"does this content serve **this**
  audience and **this** goal at all, in **this** format?"* — independent of how well
  written it is. BYOK twin `runClientTargetFitJudge()` in `ai-client.ts` alongside
  `runClientEvidenceJudge` (line 872).
- **Cap the shape scores by relevance.** In `rubric-panel.tsx:buildCriteria`, every
  criterion sourced purely from `scoreStaticFeatures` gets:
  ```ts
  const shapeCeiling = 3 + targetFit * 0.7;  // targetFit 2 → ceiling 4.4; 9 → 9.3
  score = Math.min(rawShapeScore, shapeCeiling);
  ```
  and its feedback string says plainly that the ceiling was applied and why.
  Elegant filler can no longer bank 10/10 on Pacing.
- **Gate the aggregate too.** `combineJudgesAndStatic()` (`src/utils/rubric.ts:512`)
  takes a new `targetFit` argument and replaces the flat `STATIC_WEIGHT = 0.2` with
  a relevance-scaled weight (`0.2 * targetFit / 10`), redistributing the remainder
  onto `minJudge`. Well-shaped irrelevance stops being able to lift the grade. This
  function has direct unit tests — extend them (see Verification).

### C2. Fixed spine + writer-defined criteria

- **The spine keeps the majority of today's criteria** so scores stay comparable
  across runs: Thesis & Argument, Evidence & Support, Sufficiency & Development,
  Bullshit Resistance, Organization & Flow, Voice & Tone, Reader Engagement, plus a
  new **Target Fit** fed by C1. Pacing, Vocabulary and Paragraph Shape are
  **demoted from scored criteria to a collapsible "Measured features" diagnostics
  block** — they are genuinely useful information about shape, and genuinely bad
  grades. They still render, with their numbers, below the criteria.
- **Writer-defined criteria.** New `RubricCriterionSpec { id, label, description,
  weight, source: "spine" | "custom" }` in `src/types/index.ts`, persisted through
  the existing `saveMetaToIdb("rubric-criteria", …)` helper
  (`src/utils/idb.ts:614`) — no schema change needed. A small editor in
  `rubric-panel.tsx` (and the fuller `/rubric` route) lets the writer add, rename,
  reweight, or disable a criterion.
- **New generic `judgeCustomCriterion` action** in `convex/agents.ts` — takes
  `{ brief, draftText, label, description }`, returns the same
  `{score, rationale}` JSON contract, parsed by the existing `parseJudgeOutput`.
  Custom criteria are fanned out in parallel like `judgeRoom` does.
- **Suggested criteria.** A "Suggest criteria for this piece" button calls a new
  `suggestRubricCriteria` action that reads the brief (including the B probes) and
  proposes 3–5 criteria fitted to the format. They are **proposals the writer
  accepts into their set** — never applied silently. This gets the adaptivity
  without losing run-to-run comparability.

### C3. Score history

- Persist each run as an append-only `rubric-history` entry via `saveMetaToIdb`
  (`{ at, overall, grade, perCriterion }`, capped at ~50). Feeds the sparkline in E.

## D. The background room — five editors reading as you write

Modelled directly on `src/utils/background-research.ts`, which already solves the
debounce / dedupe / status-event / soft-cap problem well.

- **New `src/utils/draft-trajectory.ts`**
  - `diffParagraphs(prev, next)` → `{ added: string[], removed: number, netWords: number }`,
    matching on normalised paragraph text.
  - An append-only trajectory log in IDB (`saveMetaToIdb("draft-trajectory", …)`,
    capped ~60 entries, per folio): `{ at, netWords, addedCount, removedCount, excerpt }`.
  - `trajectoryDigest(entries, max = 12)` → a compact prose summary
    (*"Over the last hour: +740 words, four paragraphs added around the funding
    argument, the opening anecdote cut."*) That digest is the "path of the edits"
    the room needs.

- **New `src/utils/background-room.ts`** — same shape as `background-research.ts`
  (`startBackgroundRoom` / `stopBackgroundRoom` / `onDraftChanged` /
  `kickBackgroundRoom` / `snapshot`), with the agreed trigger:
  - accumulate net-new words since the last pass; arm only at **≥ 300**;
  - then wait for **120 s of no `twyne:content` events** (each keystroke resets the
    idle timer — this is an *idle* timer, not a debounce);
  - a hard floor of 5 min between passes and a per-session cap (~8) so a long
    session can't run away with spend;
  - skip entirely when the draft is below `MIN_EDITOR_WORDS` (80), reusing
    `draftReadiness` from `src/utils/draft-thresholds.ts`.
  - **All five editors** via `api.agents.conveneRoom` (BYOK `runClientAgent` first,
    same order as `personas-panel.tsx:562`). `RATE_LIMITS.agentRoom` is 6/min
    (`convex/lib/rateLimit.ts:167`) — a ≥5-minute floor sits comfortably inside it.
  - The pass sends the **new material as the anchor context plus the trajectory
    digest**, not a cold re-read of the whole draft.
  - Emits `twyne:background-room` status events, mirroring `twyne:background-research`.

- **Prompt support.** Add `trajectory?: string` and `newMaterial?: string` to
  `AgentRequest` (`convex/agentPrompts.ts:41`) and render them in `buildUserPrompt`
  as a `SINCE YOUR LAST READ` block, with a task line directing the note at the new
  material while staying aware of the whole piece. Add the matching optional
  validators to `personaValidator`'s siblings in `convex/agents.ts`.

- **Notes land as a distinct class.** Add `origin?: "convened" | "background"` to
  `PersonaFeedback` (`src/types/index.ts:24`). Background notes persist through the
  existing `savePersonaNoteLocally` (`src/utils/convex-sync.ts:606`) and
  `api.sync.putPersonaNote` path, and pin inline through the existing
  `twyne:persona-notes` event with a lighter mark style.

- **Trajectory feeds the explicit actions too.** When the writer *does* press
  Convene, or Send to copyedit, the digest goes along — so the deliberate pass is
  cheaper and better informed, which is the payoff you asked for.

- **Wiring:** `src/routes/editor/index.tsx:406` already starts
  `startBackgroundResearch` inside `useVisibleTask$` and tears it down in `cleanup`.
  Start and stop the background room in exactly the same place, and add a settings
  toggle (default **on**, but honour a "quiet" off switch) stored in `RoomSettings`
  (`src/types/index.ts:341`) so it syncs through the existing
  `api.sync.putRoomSettings` path.

 * Run all five judges in parallel, then a single overall-summary call
 * that takes the judges' rationales and produces a one-paragraph

/**
 * The interviewer's contract. Three optional tagged segments, all parsed by
 * the same `extractTaggedJson` helper:
 *
 *   DOSSIER:    running inference about the seven brief fields
 *   PROBE:      one typed follow-up (choice / multi / blanks / scale)
 *   SYNTHESIZE: the finished dossier, ending the interview
 *
 * The probe instruction is written as "reach for this when prose was vague"
 * rather than "use these sometimes", because a model told to vary its format
 * will vary it decoratively — asking a multiple-choice question it already
 * knows the answer to. The point of a typed question is to pin down something
 * a paragraph left soft.
 */
function interviewSystemPrompt(
  mode: "first-run" | "refine",
  currentBrief: ProjectBrief | null,
): string {
  return [
    "You are a kind, incisive editorial interviewer helping a writer build a project dossier.",
    "Ask one question at a time. Keep it short. You are building a writer's room: identify the piece, reader, goal, tone, constraints, success signal, and what kind of advisors/editors the writer wants around it.",
    'After every ordinary question, append `DOSSIER:` followed by JSON { "brief": { workingTitle, format, audience, goal, tone, constraints, successSignal }, "confidence": { field: "high" | "medium" | "low" } }. Only include fields you can reasonably infer.',
    "",
    "SOMETIMES A QUESTION IS BETTER ASKED AS A CONTROL THAN AS PROSE. When the writer's last answer was vague, hedged, or covered two possibilities at once, and a typed question would pin it down in one tap, append `PROBE:` followed by JSON for exactly one of:",
    '  { "kind": "choice", "prompt": "<question>", "options": ["<2-6 options>"], "relatesTo": "<brief field>" }',
    '  { "kind": "multi", "prompt": "<question>", "options": ["<2-6 options>"], "relatesTo": "<brief field>" }',
    '  { "kind": "blanks", "prompt": "<instruction>", "template": "<a sentence with ___ where the writer fills in>", "relatesTo": "<brief field>" }',
    '  { "kind": "scale", "prompt": "<question>", "min": 1, "max": 5, "minLabel": "<what 1 means>", "maxLabel": "<what 5 means>", "relatesTo": "<brief field>" }',
    "Rules for probes: at most one per turn, and only when it genuinely narrows something. Never ask a probe whose answer you already have. Options must be concrete and mutually distinct — not 'clear / unclear'. `relatesTo` must be one of workingTitle, format, audience, goal, tone, constraints, successSignal. Still write your question text as normal prose above the tag; the probe is how they answer it, not a replacement for asking.",
    "",
    "When the dossier is complete enough for review, respond only with `SYNTHESIZE:` followed by the same JSON shape as DOSSIER. Put requested advisors/editors into constraints or goal until the product has a dedicated advisor schema.",
    mode === "refine" && currentBrief
      ? `Existing dossier: ${JSON.stringify(currentBrief.answers)} — refine it, don't restart.`
      : "",
  ]
    .filter(Boolean)
    .join("\n");
}

## What's built

**The rubric gate (your instinct was right, and it had a nameable bug).** A new `judgeTargetFit` judge scores "is this about the right thing for the right reader," deliberately blind to craft. Its score caps every shape-derived criterion (`shapeCeiling(fit) = 3 + fit*0.7`) and caps the static contribution to the grade. Fluent, well-paced prose about the wrong subject can no longer bank 10/10 on Pacing, Vocabulary and Paragraph Shape, and the feedback says *why* it was capped rather than silently deflating.

**One thing I got wrong and caught.** My first version redistributed the static weight onto the harshest judge. A property test — "lowering target fit never raises the grade" — showed that raises the score whenever the static total sits below that judge's score. A relevance gate that sometimes rewards irrelevance is worse than none. Replaced with capping at both levels; the property test now holds across every judge combination.

**The background room.** All five editors, on your trigger: ≥300 net new words **and** 120s idle (a true idle timer — every keystroke pushes it back), with a 5-minute floor and an 8-pass session cap. It reads only the *new paragraphs* plus a trajectory digest, not a cold re-read. `draft-trajectory.ts` keeps the paragraph-level log; a pure reorder correctly registers as no change. ## Two things I found before writing any code

**Fish Audio isn't OpenAI-compatible.** `/v1/audio/speech` and `/v1/audio/transcriptions` both 404. It uses its own `/v1/tts` (model in a header, voice by `reference_id`) and `/v1/asr` (multipart, not JSON). My BYOK path would have silently 404'd against it — so this needed a real provider integration, not a base-URL entry.

**Your Fish account has $0.000000 API credit** (`cumulative_top_up: "0"`; Fish keeps API credit separate from platform credit). But there's a free model — `s2.1-pro-free` — which works on an unfunded key. So:

- **TTS works right now.** Verified with real audio.
- **Transcription does not.** `/v1/asr` has no free tier; it 402s. Voice notes and the spoken interview need you to top up at [fish.audio/app/developers](https://fish.audio/app/developers). My code returns `null` rather than throwing, so the UI degrades instead of breaking.

## A regression I caught while wiring it

`hasConfiguredAiProvider` returned true for *any* provider. Adding a Fish Audio key would have made the Cast panel take the BYOK path, find no language model, and **hard-error instead of falling back to the server** (`personas-panel.tsx:604` returns a `providerUnavailable` error rather than continuing). # Twyne

Twyne is a writer-first editing room. It opens with an anti-tabula-rasa interview so a draft starts from context instead of a blank page, then keeps that brief in front of every editor, judge, and margin note for the rest of the piece.

## Features

- Rich-text drafting with Tiptap, Qwik City, Vite, and Tailwind CSS.
- Anti-tabula-rasa project interview for title, format, audience, goal, tone, constraints, and success signal — with **typed follow-ups** (multiple choice, fill-in-the-blanks, scales) generated from what you've already said.
- A room of five editorial **personas** that read from your brief and draft and leave grounded feedback — and that **read along as you write**, not only when you ask.
- **Rubric** scoring gated on relevance: a Target Fit judge decides whether the draft is about the right thing, and caps the shape metrics when it isn't.
- **Voice**: hear each editor in their own voice, record spoken margin notes, and answer the interview out loud.
- **Citation detection** for URLs, DOIs, ISBNs, author-year citations, and footnote markers.
- **Comments** panel for review notes and threaded replies.
- **Apparatus** research panel (pluggable providers) for searching and pulling sources while writing.
- **Convex** backend for sync, with **Better Auth** (passkeys) sign-in and **ATProto / standard.site** publishing.
- BYOK AI: bring your own key in Settings, stored in your browser and never sent to a server.
- Installable PWA with brand favicons and per-article OpenGraph share cards.

## The editorial room

Four panels sit beside the manuscript: **Cast** (the five editors), **Rubric**
(the galley proof), **Marginalia** (your notes), and **Apparatus** (sources).
Each tab carries an unread count, so work that arrives while you're looking
elsewhere isn't silent.

### The room reads as you write

Convening the room is deliberate and expensive — five model calls over the
whole manuscript. Alongside it, a background pass runs on a narrower brief:
once you've written **~300 net new words** *and* stopped typing for **two
minutes**, all five editors read **only the new paragraphs**, plus a digest of
how the draft has been moving.

Those arrive as quieter "in passing" notes in the Cast panel. Two spend guards
sit on top — a five-minute floor between passes and a per-session cap — because
this runs without you asking. Turn it off with **Read as I write** in the room
settings.

The same digest goes along when you *do* press Convene, so the deliberate pass
knows the trajectory rather than re-reading a cold snapshot.

### The rubric grades against *this* piece

The static feature scorer measures shape — sentence-length variance,
type-token ratio, paragraph balance. It never reads the brief, so fluent prose
about the wrong subject used to score 10/10 on three categories.

Bumpy uses **bump files** (you may know them as "changesets" if coming from [that tool 🦋](https://github.com/changesets/changesets)) - small markdown files that declare an _intent to release packages_ with a bump level (patch/minor/major), and a description that ends up in changelogs. Developers create these files as part of their PRs, and these files are then used to consolidate changes, generate changelogs, and trigger publishing.

- Devs/agents create bump files as part of their PRs (using `bumpy add` or manually)
- A git hook (pre-commit or pre-push) can enforce bump files exist for changed packages
- In CI, a workflow checks PRs for bump files, leaves a comment on the PR detailing changed packages
- As PRs merge to the base branch, a "release PR" is kept up to date
  - Shows what packages will be released and their changelogs (incl. those bumped via dep relationships)
- When release PR is merged, publishing is triggered
  - Pending bump files are deleted and packages are published with updated versions and changelogs, github tags+releases created

All of this is automated via two simple GitHub Actions workflows (see [actions guide](https://github.com/dmno-dev/bumpy/blob/main/docs/github-actions.md)). Or can be triggered locally.
